title: Can a triangle have exactly two fold lines?
description: Triangles are drawn with one fold line, with three fold lines and with none. Then the question is whether a triangle can have exactly two fold lines.
teaching_notes: One idea: the number of matching folds of a triangle depends on how many sides are equal, and two folds force a third. Watch for students who guess that a triangle with two folds exists because one and three do.

source: Draw the following. (a) A triangle with exactly one line of symmetry. (b) A triangle with exactly three lines of symmetry. (c) A triangle with no line of symmetry. Is it possible to draw a triangle with exactly two lines of symmetry?
video_script.why: The child links the number of equal sides of a triangle to its matching folds and sees why exactly two folds cannot happen.
video_script.substitution: Draw triangles with two equal sides, with all sides equal and with all sides different, and fold each one in the mind.
video_script.anchor: Three triangles to draw: one with two equal sides, one with all sides equal and one with all sides different
video_script.payoff_line: Two lines of symmetry force a third.

final_answer.value: two equal sides: one line; all sides equal: three lines; all sides different: none; exactly two lines: not possible
final_answer.spoken: a triangle with two equal sides has one line, with all sides equal has three, and with all sides different has none, and exactly two is not possible

never_show: the verdict on exactly two lines before the answer beat
maths_rules: A line of symmetry is a fold line along which one half covers the other exactly.
A triangle with exactly two equal sides has exactly one line, from the corner where the equal sides meet to the middle of the third side.
A triangle with all three sides equal has three lines, one from each corner to the middle of the opposite side.
A triangle with all sides different has no line.
If a triangle had two lines, then two pairs of sides would be equal, which makes all three sides equal and gives three lines. So exactly two lines is not possible.
Check: count the folds again on each drawn triangle.
video_script.design: One idea: matching folds of a triangle follow its equal sides. Assumes the child has the fold test. The three drawn triangles stay on the board from the hook to the end.
